listenings.text: Hello everyone, I am Sophie. I live in Manchester, but this month I am staying in an apartment above a bakery two streets from here, and I wake up smelling bread every morning. I am teaching a summer drawing course for two weeks, so I am here until the end of the month. I do not know anybody in this town yet. Actually, I think nobody at this table knows anybody, so at least we all have that in common. Please tell me your names, and where you are staying.

After twenty years of travelling alone, I have three rules for talking to strangers. First, choose the person who is looking at something, not the person who is looking at a phone. Someone studying a wall or a map is already curious, and curious people answer. Second, never ask do you like it here. The answer is yes, and then the conversation is over. Ask what brings you here instead, because that one needs a story. Third, give one small thing about yourself before you ask a second question, so the other person has something to hold on to. That is all. It works in every country I have ever visited.

extra_audio.text: He noticed that the woman at the next table was looking at the wall, not at the sea. He was curious, so he approached her and asked if she was an architect. She said she restores old stone buildings in Chicago, so they had something in common. She said her grandfather was born an hour from there, so she is spending three weeks in Croatia. He said that was fascinating and asked her to tell him more about it.
